newsitem.title: USA: Clinton to discuss economy, environment in Australia.
newsitem.headline: Clinton to discuss economy, environment in Australia.

text.p: President Bill Clinton, on his first trip abroad since his re-election, on Monday was set to begin a four-day state visit to Australia focusing on economic and environmental issues.

After a golfing weekend in Hawaii that was interrupted on Sunday when a Russian spacecraft tumbled from the skies and for a time seemed likely to crash to Earth in Australia, Clinton was to arrive in Sydney on Tuesday evening after crossing the international dateline on a 10-hour flight.
The errant six-tonne spacecraft wound up splashing harmlessly into the Pacific Ocean somewhere west of Chile.

Clinton, the third American president to visit Australia after Lyndon Johnson and George Bush, was to fly to the capital Canberra after a night's sleep and plunge into an official schedule that included talks with Prime Minister John Howard and a speech to Parliament.

U.S. officials said Clinton's visit was designed to reaffirm bonds of friendship between the United States and Australia that have existed for more than 200 years. They said that in his speech to Parliament he would thank Australia for its help in achieving the Comprehensive Nuclear Test Ban Treaty and its cooperation on World Trade Organisation issues.

On a 1992 visit to Australia, Bush ran into noisy demonstrations by wheat farmers protesting a U.S. trade programme -- the Export Enhancement Programme -- that protesters said unfairly subsidised U.S. grain sales.

Clinton, whose schedule also included ceremonial wreath-layings, a Sydney harbour cruise and a round of golf with Australian pro Greg Norman, was to tour the Great Barrier Reef later this week and talk about the need to preserve such priceless natural resources, the White House said.

The north Queensland area where the reef is located has a special significance for Americans because it served as a staging area for the Battle of the Coral Sea in the Second World War, the first major U.S. military victory over Japan and a turning point in the war in the Pacific.

From Australia, Clinton will go to the Philippines for the annual Asian trade summit next weekend, which will focus on how to implement a plan to create a free trade zone throughout the Pacific rim region by 2010. Clinton was to visit Thailand afterwards and return to the United States on Nov. 27.
